prompt.context: Your client is a U.S. state's social services agency. The agency is responsible for administering the state's social work programs. Recently, the state legislature passed a law that will change the agency's funding structure. Previously, the agency had been funded at a fixed dollar amount. Now, under the new law, the agency will be paid according to performance, as measured by the number of interviews they conduct with state social work clients. The agency has hired you to determine how the change will affect them and what they should do about it.
prompt.question: How will the funding change affect the agency, and what should they do about it?

clarifying_info.q: What activities does the agency perform?
clarifying_info.a: For the purpose of simplicity, the agency's only activity is conducting interviews.

clarifying_info.q: How was the agency previously funded?
clarifying_info.a: Previously, the agency received $50,000 per employee per year.

clarifying_info.q: How much of that cost went to salary vs. overhead?
clarifying_info.a: On average $30,000 went to salary and $20,000 went to overhead.

clarifying_info.q: How many employees does the agency have?
clarifying_info.a: Unknown. This case is on a per-employee basis.

clarifying_info.q: How will the agency be funded under the new law?
clarifying_info.a: The agency will be paid $25 per interview.

clarifying_info.q: How many interviews does each social worker conduct per day?
clarifying_info.a: Currently each social worker conducts an average of 5 interviews per day.

clarifying_info.q: Can the agency increase the number of interviews per social worker per day?
clarifying_info.a: Under the current system, the agency could boost the number of interviews from 5 to 6 per day.

clarifying_info.q: How long does it currently take to conduct an interview?
clarifying_info.a: It takes one hour; 40 minutes is the interview and 20 minutes is follow-up data entry.

clarifying_info.q: Is there any way to reduce the 20-minute data entry time?
clarifying_info.a: The agency has found a very inexpensive transcription software program that would allow them to cut the 20 minutes to 10.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other ways to increase the number of interviews beyond 7 per day?
clarifying_info.a: There is no other way to squeeze more interviews in a day.

clarifying_info.q: Is there private charitable funding available?
clarifying_info.a: The agency can garner $1,000 per employee per year from a private charitable trust.

clarifying_info.q: Can the agency merge some of its facilities with other state agencies to reduce overhead?
clarifying_info.a: Yes, the agency can consolidate its offices into other state agency buildings at a savings of $4,000 per employee per year.

clarifying_info.q: Are all social workers paid evenly?
clarifying_info.a: No. 30% are paid $25K/year, 40% are paid $30K/year, and 30% are paid $35K/year. The agency can convert half of the workers at the highest pay grade to the lowest pay grade.

framework: Understand the previous funding structure (revenue per employee under fixed funding)
Understand the new funding structure (revenue per interview × interviews per day × work days)
Quantify the budget shortfall under the new system
Identify revenue-side levers to close the gap (increase interview volume, seek alternative funding)
Identify cost-side levers to close the gap (reduce overhead, restructure salaries)
Summarize and recommend a combined action plan

questions.prompt: Calculate annual revenue per employee under the new funding structure if the agency continues to operate as before (5 interviews/day).
questions.guidance: Multiply work days × interviews per day × rate per interview. Compare to previous funding of $50,000 per employee to identify the shortfall.

math.answer: $31,250 revenue; $18,750 budget shortfall per employee per year

questions.prompt: If the agency pushes daily interviews from 5 to 6 per social worker, what is the new revenue and remaining shortfall?
questions.guidance: Recalculate annual revenue at 6 interviews/day and compare to $50,000.

steps: Remaining shortfall = $50,000 − $37,500 = $12,500 per employee per year
math.answer: $37,500 revenue; $12,500 shortfall per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency adopts transcription software that cuts data entry from 20 minutes to 10 minutes per interview. How does this change interview capacity and revenue?
questions.guidance: Calculate time saved per day across 6 interviews, convert to additional interview slots, then recalculate revenue.

math.setup: 10 min saved × 6 interviews/day = 60 min saved = 1 extra interview/day → 7 interviews/day; 250 × 7 × $25
steps: 10 min saved per interview × 6 interviews = 60 minutes freed per day
Remaining shortfall = $50,000 − $43,750 = $6,250 per employee per year
math.answer: $43,750 revenue; $6,250 shortfall per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency secures $1,000 per employee per year from a private charitable trust. What is the remaining gap?
questions.guidance: Subtract charitable funding from current shortfall.

math.answer: $5,250 remaining shortfall per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency consolidates offices with other state agencies, saving $4,000 per employee per year in overhead. What gap remains?
questions.guidance: Subtract the overhead savings from the remaining shortfall.

math.answer: $1,250 remaining shortfall per employee per year

questions.prompt: The agency restructures salaries: 30% at $25K, 40% at $30K, 30% at $35K. Half the workers at $35K are converted to $25K. What are the new salary distribution and savings?
questions.guidance: Recalculate the salary mix and compute the blended savings per employee. The savings eliminate the remaining shortfall and produce a small surplus.

math.setup: Half of 30% (i.e., 15%) move from $35K to $25K; new mix: 45% at $25K, 40% at $30K, 15% at $35K; savings = 15% × ($35K − $25K)
steps: Original top tier: 30% at $35K; half converted → 15% move to $25K
Net position = −$1,250 + $1,500 = +$250 surplus per employee per year
math.answer: $1,500 salary savings; net surplus of $250 per employee per year (some of which can fund the new IT/transcription system)

brainstorming.prompt: What are the different ways the agency could close a budget shortfall resulting from the funding change?

categories.name: Increase interview volume
ideas: Push interviews per day from 5 to 6 through scheduling optimization
Adopt transcription software to cut data entry from 20 to 10 minutes, enabling a 7th interview per day
Reduce non-interview administrative burdens on social workers
Hire part-time or contract workers during peak demand periods

categories.name: Seek alternative revenue sources
ideas: Solicit private charitable trust donations ($1,000/employee/year identified)
Apply for federal grants tied to social service performance
Partner with nonprofits who can co-fund certain program activities

categories.name: Reduce overhead costs
ideas: Consolidate office space with other state agencies ($4,000/employee/year saving identified)
Reduce utility and facilities costs through energy efficiency
Centralize shared administrative functions across state agencies

categories.name: Reduce salary costs
ideas: Convert highest-paid workers (30% at $35K) to lower pay grades where feasible
Freeze merit increases until budget gap is closed
Offer voluntary early retirement to higher-paid senior staff

recommendation: The funding change will create an $18,750 per-employee per-year budget shortfall if the agency continues operating as before.

By combining five levers — increasing interviews to 7/day via transcription software (+$12,500 revenue), securing charitable funding (+$1,000), consolidating office space (−$4,000 costs), and restructuring salaries (−$1,500 costs) — the agency can fully close the gap and achieve a small $250/employee/year surplus.
risks: Transcription software adoption may take time and training, delaying the revenue impact
Salary restructuring may affect staff morale and retention, especially for high performers
Charitable funding is not guaranteed year-over-year and introduces revenue volatility
Office consolidation with other agencies may reduce operational independence or create coordination friction
next_steps: Procure and roll out the transcription software immediately to capture the efficiency gain
Negotiate office-sharing arrangements with other state agencies
Implement salary restructuring in consultation with HR and labor counsel
Pursue and formalize the charitable trust funding agreement
Monitor interview volume and per-employee revenue monthly to track performance under the new funding model
